subject: Solstice-6B-mix: tokenizer/kv compatibility & provisional pin request
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Solstice-6B-mix: tokenizer/kv compatibility & provisional pin request

Team — quick heads up. Helia (external) pushed a new variant labeled Solstice-6B-mix that claims a smaller tokenizer footprint and a modified KV prefetch pattern. We spun a quick smoke yesterday against staging and observed two issues: 1) tokenization skew on some punctuation-heavy prompts (diff attached), and 2) a small but reproducible increase in KV cache misses that spikes tail-latency on long context flows.

Context / ask: AcmeApp (Maria) is onboarding Solstice for their customer-facing chat; they requested a targeted rollout next week. Given the risk, I want to request a provisional version pin for Solstice-6B-mix on the AcmeApp route until we can sign off the tokenizer mapping and KV behavior. Practically: block auto-roll to this variant for their account and route to Solstice-6B-v2 (previously validated) as fallback.

What I need from you:
- Priyom: product decision on whether we can grant a short-term pin (48–72h) and any commercial communication to AcmeApp.
- Monica: short compatibility triage + ETA for a deeper behavioral test (tokenization + KV telemetry). Can you confirm whether the tokenizer table change is safe for existing embeddings/semantic-search index compatibility?
- Lauren: operational lift — can you create a temporary route-level pin and a canary that preserves logs at DEBUG for this tenant? Also confirm rollback steps.

Attachments: solstice-6b-vocab-diff.txt, kv-cache-behavior-notes.md

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Technical Program Manager, Inference
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Solstice-6B-mix: tokenizer/kv compatibility & provisional pin request

+1 on conservative approach. Rafael — I support a provisional pin for AcmeApp for 72 hours while we validate. A couple of product questions before I green-light:

1) Is this variant tagged "recommended" in Helia's catalog or experimental? (If recommended, we should pause only for this tenant; if experimental, consider a broader hold.)
2) Are there any contractual obligations (SLA/uptime window) that would make a pin problematic for AcmeApp? David, can you confirm there are no active SLOs tied to the variant rollout?

If we proceed, messaging to AcmeApp should be: transparent but short — "we're pausing the variant rollout for your tenant while we complete compatibility checks; you'll remain on the currently validated variant with no interruption". I'll draft a one-paragraph line to use.

Priyom
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-02T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Solstice-6B-mix: tokenizer/kv compatibility & provisional pin request

Quick triage notes from the smoke: attaching a short PDF with test output (compat-smoke-report.pdf). Headline items: 

- Tokenizer: the new vocab mapping drops two multi-byte punctuation tokens and merges them with a fallback token. That changes token boundary counts for ~0.4% of our long-tail prompts — mostly punctuation-heavy system messages. This will affect exact-match embedding keys if customers depend on deterministic tokenization for cached retrieval.
- KV cache: the variant introduces a lazy-Prefetch path for KV which defers loading of some segments to generation time; that reduces steady-state memory but increases variance in KV misses for sequences >1024. Median latency unchanged; 95th/99th increased by ~8–12% in our synthetic long-context flows.

Next steps & ETA: I can run a focused embedding-regeneration test for AcmeApp's top-100 prompt set and a telemetry sweep across their recent 7-day production traffic. I expect the smoke -> full check to take ~36 hours (run today + morning run tomorrow) assuming we can preserve DEBUG traces for that tenant (Lauren).

Recommendations:
- Approve 72h provisional pin for AcmeApp on Solstice-6B-v2 and enable DEBUG traces.
- If tokenization differences invalidate any semantic-search keys for AcmeApp, schedule an embedding refresh job (we can offer to run it as part of onboarding).

I'll start the test now and post results as soon as the sweep completes.

—Monica
Staff Applied ML Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-02T12:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Solstice-6B-mix: tokenizer/kv compatibility & provisional pin request

On it — I will:
- Create a tenant-scoped route pin for AcmeApp to Solstice-6B-v2 (expires after 72 hours unless extended).
- Enable DEBUG-level KV/tokenization traces for that tenant and persist logs to long-term bucket for the next 7 days.
- Add an automated rollback route that flips the tenant back to Solstice-6B-v2 if 95th P99 latency crosses our pre-agreed threshold (15% over baseline) — manual approval required to lift the pin.

I will create the change request in Jira (RINF-3241) and link the DocuSign approval stub in case legal/product want to authorize communications to Acme.

Lauren
Staff Site Reliability Engineer, Inference
Redwood Inference

From: Sam Torres <sam@helia.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maria Lopez <maria@acmeapp.com>
Date: 2028-03-02T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Solstice-6B-mix: tokenizer/kv compatibility & provisional pin request

Thanks for the heads up and for running the checks. Quick notes from Helia: the Solstice-6B-mix tokenizer change was intended to be a lossless remap for UTF punctuation, but we see the same merge on our side in internal QA and will ship a micro-patch today to restore backward-compatible token boundaries. I'll send a diff and a signed artifact (DocuSign stub attached) once the micro-patch is available.

For the KV prefetch: that was a configurable runtime flag in our release; we can provide a build with eager-prefetch enabled for your cluster to match the previous behavior. If Redwood wants to keep the lazy-prefetch as default, we can include a compatibility shim that replicates prior cache behavior for pinned tenants.

We appreciate the conservative approach. I'll upload the micro-patch artifacts here: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/solstice-6b/compat-smoke-report.pdf and notify when doc/signature is ready.

—Sam
Head of Integrations
HeliaAI
